messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Edge authz anomaly detected — AUTH-EDGE-401-ANOMALY. 401 rate spike from 18.52.34.0/24 to auth-proxy (3.2k/min). Pager routed to oncall (alice.sre).

alice.sre: acked — I'm on it. pulling recent proxy logs and checking upstream tokens.

alice.sre: quick triage: spike is mostly 401s, not 5xx. Many requests include an `x-api-key` header with similar prefix. Looks like a replay/noise source rather than backend failure.

chandra-eng-platform: can you paste a sample log line? I'll check edge ACLs and our WAF.

alice.sre: ```
time=2026-03-17T02:12:03Z src=18.52.34.12 method=POST path=/v1/internal/auth x-api-key=mon-XXXXXX-abcdef status=401 UA="curl/7.68"
time=2026-03-17T02:12:04Z src=18.52.34.45 method=POST path=/v1/internal/auth x-api-key=mon-XXXXXX-abcdef status=401 UA="python-requests/2.25"
```

ben.security: Ben here. Suggest immediate WAF block for 18.52.34.0/24 and rotate the service account token used by `svc-integ-monitor`. Possible misconfigured third-party monitoring or compromised monitor.

dana-cs: any customer impact seen in metrics/alerts?

alice.sre: CS note: we see ~12 customers with elevated auth failures (background jobs reporting 401) in last 10m. No 500s reported and no user data access attempts logged.

alice.sre: mitigation plan (short):
1) Push WAF rule to block 18.52.34.0/24 at edge (chandra)
2) Disable `svc-integ-monitor` webhook/ingress (alice + chandra)
3) Rotate keys for `svc-integ-monitor` (ben) and revoke old tokens
4) CS to draft customer comms and optionally invalidate sessions for the few affected clients (dana)
5) Forensics: search logs for cleartext tokens and exfil patterns (alice/ben)

chandra-eng-platform: pushing WAF rule now, will stream deploy status. ETA ~30s.
deploy-bot: WAF rule deployment: version=2026-03-17-0545-2 status=success target=edge-north-1

chandra-eng-platform: block applied — traffic from 18.52.34.0/24 dropped at edge.

alice.sre: after block, 401 rate back to baseline (dropped ~95%). still collecting full request bodies for forensics; saving a 30m capture.

ben.security: starting rotation for svc-integ-monitor keys now. Will revoke and issue new short-lived credentials, update terraform/state, and coordinate with partner. ETA ~10m.

dana-cs: prepping top-affected customer emails: short template ready ("transient auth errors, mitigation in progress, no evidence of data exfiltration so far"). sending to top-5 now.

alice.sre: CS note received. Please include support link and incident contact.

eric-legal: keep me posted on any confirmed token leakage or PII access. We may need to escalate to formal notice depending on forensic findings.

alice.sre: preliminary forensics: found repeated token string in a handful of log lines — looks like the integration used a long-lived key in the header. No downstream credential use beyond the observed 18.52.34.x calls. Still scanning s3 log buckets for accidental leak.

ben.security: rotation complete, old tokens revoked. Coordinate with partner to confirm they reconfigure to short-lived tokens. Recommend we require scoped short-lived tokens for integrations going forward.

alice.sre: handoff: I'll hand this to night oncall in 20m — @kevin-oncall will pick up monitoring and follow through with forensics and postmortem. Keep this thread for updates.

kevin-oncall: ack. I'll watch the auth dashboards and grep logs for token occurrences. ping me if new IP ranges show up.

alice.sre: summary for the record: suspected cause — misconfigured third-party monitor calling internal auth endpoint with long-lived key causing credential replay/noise and client 401s. Immediate mitigations: edge WAF block, disabled integration, rotated service token, notified affected customers. No confirmed data exfil at this time. Postmortem + remediation (enforce short-lived tokens, alerting on unusual header reuse) to follow. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident routed to `incidents` and recorded. Next steps: add to postmortem queue and schedule follow-up with security + platform.
